final.memo:
We have long admired the franchise built by Bank of America, which serves as a significant depository institution with durable scale [D01]. Our initial investment, secured through preferreds and warrants, served us well, but our current common equity position is a residual claim [D01]. 

With our stake exceeding 10%, we are subject to rigorous insider transaction reporting requirements [D08]. Reducing this holding toward the 10% threshold simplifies our regulatory footprint and reporting obligations, a prudent step regardless of our high regard for the underlying business [D08]. 

We do not sell wonderful businesses without cause, but we are mindful of the tax costs—currently 21% federal—associated with pruning a position that has appreciated since our initial investment [S3]. This reduction is a matter of administrative and portfolio management rather than a change in the fundamental economics of the bank, which continues to generate respectable returns on tangible equity [D03].
uncited_claims: The decision to trim is driven by the desire to stay just under the 10% regulatory ownership threshold, consistent with past practice in major bank holdings like Wells Fargo.
